INSIGHTS

Thinking Forward

Insights on AI, technology, investing, and what comes next.

AI & BUILDING 04 MIN READ

AI is moving from feature to infrastructure

The real shift is not another AI feature. It is the redesign of how products, teams, and decisions operate.

Read article

The first generation of AI products focused on adding intelligence to an existing workflow. The more interesting opportunity comes next: rebuilding the workflow so intelligence is present from the start.

That changes the product question from “Where can we add AI?” to “What should this system do differently because intelligence is now abundant?” The answer can create better economics, faster feedback, and stronger user value.

INVESTING 03 MIN READ

The investor’s edge is often better questions

Strong decisions rarely begin with a prediction. They begin with a sharper way of framing the opportunity.

Read article

Before asking whether an asset will rise, ask what creates its value, what can break the thesis, and which assumptions matter most.

Good research reduces noise. Good questions make the remaining signal easier to see.

TECH & STRATEGY 03 MIN READ

Build for leverage, not noise

The best systems make a small team more capable without making the business more complicated.

Read article

Leverage comes from reusable systems, automation, distribution, and better decision loops—not from adding complexity for its own sake.

The goal is simple: create an engine where each improvement makes the next improvement easier.

AI & BUILDING 04 MIN READ

AI-native products are built around loops

The strongest AI products improve through repeated feedback, not one-off features.

Read article

A useful AI product creates a loop between action, feedback, and improvement. Each cycle should make the system more useful without adding friction for the user.

That is where defensibility can emerge: not from a single model call, but from the product learning how to deliver a better outcome every time.

INVESTING 03 MIN READ

Clarity matters before consensus

The opportunity is often hiding in what the market has not framed clearly yet.

Read article

Consensus can be useful, but it is rarely the edge. The better starting point is understanding what the market believes, why it believes it, and which assumption is most fragile.

Clear thinking turns uncertainty into a set of questions you can test instead of a story you simply accept.

TECH & STRATEGY 03 MIN READ

The best tools disappear into the workflow

Great software feels less like another app and more like an invisible advantage.

Read article

The best tools remove steps, compress feedback cycles, and quietly improve decisions. Their value is measured by what the user can accomplish, not by how much interface they expose.

When technology becomes infrastructure for the workflow, adoption becomes habit—and the system compounds in value as the team uses it.
